transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Um, well, I came in because I keep having these... these really nagging thoughts about my work. I'm a graphic designer, and honestly, lately the whole process has just been so chaotic. Like, the new software updates they keep pushing out? Total nightmare. I spent half of Tuesday just trying to find where they moved my usual tools, and my cat, Barnaby, kept jumping on my desk while I was working, which didn't help at all. He actually knocked over a fern I just bought at the farmer's market. 

But, um, anyway, what I meant was... I keep getting stuck on this idea that I've missed some tiny mistake in a layout, or like I've accidentally sent the wrong version of a file to a client. And the thing is, even when I look at the screen and I can see it's probably completely fine, my mind just keeps circling back to it over and over. It’s just... it won't let it go. Kind of like how my sister wouldn't let go of wanting to use the Papyrus font for her wedding invites last year, which was a whole other disaster I had to fix... but yeah, that's mostly why I made the appointment.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work to try and get rid of these nagging thoughts?

Yeah, I do. It’s like... before I submit any work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare all the layers, re-save it just to be absolutely sure. Which, honestly, dealing with layers lately is a huge pain because of that software update I mentioned earlier. I was doing this trifold brochure for a local bakery on Wednesday—oh, they have the most amazing lavender honey cupcakes, by the way. I actually bought a dozen for my niece’s birthday last weekend. She just turned seven, and she wanted this whole elaborate mermaid theme. Let me tell you, trying to find mermaid party supplies that don't look completely tacky and cheap is basically a full-time job. I ended up having to custom print half the decorations myself just so the color palette wouldn't clash. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the checking. So yeah, I’ll re-save the file and then sometimes I just sit there and mentally walk through every single design choice one more time in my head. It’s not like it takes over my entire day or anything, but it definitely makes me a lot slower. I just feel less free creatively, you know? Like I'm too bogged down in double-checking everything to actually just let go and design.
Do you experience these nagging thoughts or feelings of anxiety when you're not working or thinking about work?

Um, no, not really. When I'm not working, I'm actually pretty relaxed. Like on the weekends, I try to completely disconnect from my screens. I’ve actually been getting really into balcony gardening lately to sort of decompress. My apartment faces south, so it gets this incredible afternoon light, and I started growing these heirloom tomatoes—Cherokee Purples, I think they're called? 

But oh my gosh, the aphids this year are completely out of control. I was reading on this gardening blog that you can use neem oil to get rid of them, but let me tell you, it smells absolutely terrible. Kind of like rancid garlic and sulfur? My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, actually complained about the smell in the hallway, which is completely ridiculous because she boils cabbage literally every Thursday night and I never say a word about it. I just light a candle and mind my own business. She's always been a little prickly, though, ever since the building management changed last fall. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the thoughts. Yeah, no, I don't really get that nagging feeling about other stuff. It's pretty much just the design files and my work.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are affecting your overall well-being or relationships outside of work?

Um, my relationships outside of work are mostly fine, like I said. But my overall well-being... I mean, I guess it's taking a toll on me at the office. I’m still getting my actual work done, but I’ve started missing our internal deadlines. We have this project manager, Greg, who is a total stickler for timelines. He sends these passive-aggressive Slack messages with the little turtle emoji when you're late. Which, honestly, I don't even know why they made the turtle emoji look so judgmental in the new software update. It used to be cute! I actually had a pet turtle when I was a kid, Michelangelo. We kept him in this glass tank in the kitchen, but my mom made us get rid of him because she read an article about salmonella in a magazine at the dentist's office. She’s always been a bit of a hypochondriac, honestly. She still won't eat at salad bars.

But um... sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, my work. Yeah, so I'm missing those internal deadlines with Greg, and I've also noticed I'm really holding back on bolder design ideas lately. I just end up playing it really safe because I’m so afraid I’ll overlook something and make a mistake. And I really, really don't want to damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role. The position is actually opening up next spring because our current director is moving to Portland to roast his own coffee beans or something, which is so cliché for a designer, but good for him, I guess. But yeah, I just... I worry I'm ruining my shot at the promotion because I'm too stuck in my head to just do my best work.
Do you feel like these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?

Um, distress? I mean, I guess a little? It's frustrating, for sure. But I wouldn't say I'm like, losing sleep over it or crying in my car. Actually, speaking of my car, I just had to take it in for an oil change yesterday, and the mechanic told me I need all new brake pads. Which is ridiculous because I just got them replaced like, what, two years ago? And I barely even drive that much since we switched to a hybrid schedule at work. I only go into the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays now. 

Thursdays are actually the worst commute, though, because of that farmer's market they set up on 4th Street. It completely blocks off my usual shortcut. Though, I will say, they have this one stand that sells these incredible artisanal cheeses. I bought this truffle gouda last week that was just out of this world. I tried making a grilled cheese with it, but I totally burned the sourdough bread because I was distracted watching this documentary about octopuses. Did you know they have three hearts? It's wild. They're so smart, they can unscrew jars from the inside. 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Distress? Yeah, um, no, it's not a huge amount of distress. It's just annoying. Like, a mild annoyance that I can't just be quick and confident with my designs anymore. It's not ruining my life or anything.
How long have you been experiencing these nagging thoughts about your work?

Um, how long? I'm not entirely sure, honestly. I feel like it's been a while, maybe? Time is so weird lately. I was just talking to my sister about this over the weekend. We went to this new brunch place downtown—The Rusty Spoon, I think it's called? They have these amazing mimosa flights, but the wait was literally an hour and a half. We ended up standing outside in the cold, and I forgot my good coat because I was rushing to leave the house. I bought this beautiful wool blend trench coat last month from a vintage shop, and it's perfect for this weather, but the dry cleaner totally ruined the lining. I mean, who uses high heat on vintage wool? It's just common sense. I tried to complain to the manager, but he just gave me this blank stare and offered me a ten percent discount on my next visit. Like I'm ever going back there! I had to leave a terrible Yelp review, which I never do, but I felt like it was my civic duty, you know? People need to be warned. 

But um, wait, sorry... how long have the thoughts been happening? Yeah, I don't really know exactly when it started. I haven't really kept track of it. It just sort of... crept up on me, I guess?
Are you finding it difficult to enjoy your hobbies, like balcony gardening, because of these nagging thoughts?

Um, my balcony gardening? No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy it when I get out there. The thoughts don't really bother me when I'm dealing with the plants. Actually, I was just out there this morning watering my new string of pearls. Have you ever grown succulents? They are so finicky! Everyone says they're the easiest plants to keep alive, but I swear, if you look at them wrong, they just shrivel up. I bought this one from a little nursery out in the suburbs, and the woman working there told me to only water it when the pearls look slightly deflated. Which is such a weird description, right? It makes me think of those sad, leftover balloons from a birthday party. 

Speaking of birthdays, my niece is turning seven next week, and my sister is throwing her this massive mermaid-themed party. She asked me to design the invitations, which was fun, but she wanted all this glitter on them. Do you know how hard it is to find a printer that will actually do foil stamping and glitter without charging an arm and a leg? I spent three hours on the phone with different print shops. One guy actually hung up on me when I asked if they used eco-friendly glitter. I mean, it's a valid question! Microplastics are a huge problem in the ocean, and it's a mermaid party, so it felt hypocritical to use regular glitter. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, the gardening. Yeah, no, the gardening is fine. The thoughts don't really mess with that. I still like doing it.
Are you finding it hard to spend time with friends and family because of these thoughts about your work?

Um, spend time with friends and family? No, I wouldn't say it's hard. I mean, I still see them. The thoughts about work don't really stop me from hanging out. Like, I'm still going to my niece's mermaid party next week, obviously. I wouldn't miss it. Though, honestly, I'm a little dreading the food situation. My sister hired this caterer who specializes in "under the sea" themed snacks, which sounds cute, but apparently, it means everything is dyed blue. Blue cupcakes, blue punch, blue pasta salad. Who wants to eat blue pasta? It just looks like a science experiment gone wrong. 

I remember when we were kids, my mom tried to make us green eggs and ham for Dr. Seuss's birthday, and I flat out refused to eat it. I just couldn't get past the color. It's funny how visual we are with food, right? As a designer, I think about color theory all the time, and blue is literally an appetite suppressant. It's why you never see fast-food logos in blue. They always use red and yellow because it makes you hungry and want to eat quickly. It's fascinating how our brains are wired to react to color like that. I was actually reading this article the other day about how painting your bedroom a certain shade of blue can lower your heart rate. I've been thinking about repainting my guest room, actually. Right now it's this awful mustard yellow that the previous owners chose, and it just feels so aggressive when you walk in. 

But um... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, friends and family. Yeah, no, I'm not avoiding them or anything. The work stuff is just... work stuff. It doesn't really get in the way of seeing people.
Are you finding that your work performance or overall functioning is significantly impacted by these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um, my work performance? I mean, I am still getting my work done. But I have started holding back on my bolder design ideas lately. Which is frustrating because I really want to move toward a creative director role. Our current creative director, Marcus, is actually stepping down next year. He is moving to Portland to open a sustainable coffee shop, which is just so cliché. A designer moving to the Pacific Northwest to roast beans. He has already started wearing these tiny knit beanies to the office and talking about flavor profiles during our morning stand-ups. It drives everyone crazy. He spent twenty minutes yesterday explaining the difference between washed and natural coffee beans when we were supposed to be reviewing a major rebrand. I was so embarrassed for him. The client has this really harsh geometric logo, and I originally wanted to pitch a softer serif font to them, but... 

Wait, sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask? Oh, right, my work. Yeah, so because I am so afraid that I will overlook something and completely damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role, I just play it safe. And I have started missing internal deadlines because I get so caught up in making sure everything is perfect before I show it to anyone. But the final work always gets done, so I guess it could be worse.
Would you say that these nagging thoughts about your work are causing you a significant amount of distress?

Um, distress? I mean, I guess it's stressful, but I wouldn't say it's like, ruining my life or anything. It's just annoying. Like, I get annoyed with myself. But it's not like I'm having a breakdown over it. It's just this constant buzzing in the back of my head. Like when a fluorescent light is flickering? We had one of those in the breakroom at work for like, three weeks, and it drove me absolutely insane. It was this low, humming noise, and nobody else seemed to notice it, or if they did, they just ignored it. I ended up putting in like four different maintenance requests, and the building manager finally came up to fix it. He was this older guy, super gruff, and he told me I just had sensitive ears. Sensitive ears! I'm a designer, I notice things. It's my job to notice things that are out of place or annoying. Speaking of annoying, the new espresso machine they put in there? It's one of those pod things, and it creates so much plastic waste. I brought it up at the last all-hands meeting, and Marcus—the coffee guy I was telling you about—actually agreed with me for once. He said we should switch to a French press system, which, honestly, would take way too much time in the morning. Can you imagine twenty people trying to use a French press before a 9 AM meeting? It would be a bloodbath. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, distress. Yeah, I mean, it's a little distressing, but it's manageable. I'm not, like, losing sleep over it or anything. It's just... there.
Can you estimate approximately how many months you've been experiencing these nagging thoughts about your work?

Um, how many months? Gosh, I'm not really sure. I haven't been keeping a calendar or anything. It feels like it's just been a while, you know? Time is so weird lately anyway. Ever since I turned forty, I feel like months just evaporate. I was talking to my friend Sarah about this—she just turned forty-two, and we were saying how it feels like we were just celebrating her thirtieth in Vegas. We went to this amazing hotel, the one with the huge fountain show? And we had this incredible dinner at a steakhouse where the waiter brought out this massive dessert tower that looked like a modern art sculpture. It had spun sugar that looked like glass. Honestly, as a designer, I was more impressed by the presentation than the taste. The structural integrity of that sugar was wild. 

I've actually been trying to incorporate more sculptural elements into my packaging designs lately. I pitched this really cool folded-paper concept for a luxury skincare line, kind of origami-inspired. It would unfold like a lotus flower when you open the box. The client loved the mock-up, but the production costs were just astronomical. The printers were quoting us these ridiculous numbers because it required hand-assembly for every single unit. Which, I get it, labor is expensive, but it just broke my heart to have to scale it back to a standard magnetic closure box. It's so boring. Magnetic closures are everywhere now. It's like the default for anything "premium." 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, how long the thoughts have been happening. Yeah, I honestly don't have an exact number for you. I haven't really been tracking it. It's just been going on for a bit.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors when you have these nagging thoughts about your work, such as arranging objects in a certain way or repeating certain actions?

Um, rituals? Like arranging things? No, not really arranging objects on my desk or anything like that. My desk is actually a mess right now. I have all these Pantone swatch books piled up because we're trying to nail down this exact shade of chartreuse for a beverage client. Chartreuse is such a tricky color. If you go too yellow, it looks like a highlighter, and if you go too green, it just looks like split pea soup. I was trying to explain this to the client on a Zoom call yesterday, and of course, my cat, Barnaby, decides that's the perfect moment to jump on my keyboard and show his tail to the entire executive team. He's a Maine Coon mix, so he's massive. He knocked over my water glass, which thankfully was almost empty, but it still made this huge clatter. The client thought it was hilarious, but I was mortified. I had to spend the next five minutes apologizing and trying to wrangle a twenty-pound furball who just wanted to chew on my microphone cord. He has this obsession with cords. I've had to replace my phone charger like three times this year because he just bites right through the casing. I tried spraying that bitter apple stuff on them, but I swear he actually likes the taste of it. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, behaviors when I have the thoughts. Yeah, so I don't arrange things, but before I submit my work now, I do this thing where I'll re-open the file, compare all the layers, re-save it, and then I kind of mentally walk through every single design choice I made one more time. It doesn't, like, take over my entire day, but it definitely makes me slower. And like I said before, it just makes me less free creatively. I'm so busy double-checking everything that I just don't take risks anymore.
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or check things in a specific way when you're having these nagging thoughts about your work?

Um, wait, didn't we just... I feel like I just said this, didn't I? About checking things? Yeah, I was just saying that before I submit my work, I have to re-open the file. And then I compare all the layers, re-save it, and kind of mentally walk through every single design choice I made one more time. It's like I have to justify every pixel to myself before I can let it go. 

Speaking of pixels, the resolution on the new monitors they bought us at work is incredible, but the color calibration was completely off when they arrived. I had to spend an entire afternoon calibrating mine because everything looked slightly magenta. And if there's one thing I can't stand, it's a magenta cast on skin tones. It makes everyone look like they have a sunburn. I was working on this campaign for a summer clothing line, and the models already looked a little too tan, so adding a magenta cast just made them look like lobsters. I actually had to go back to the photographer and ask for the raw files because the retoucher had pushed the saturation way too far. Retouchers these days, I swear, they just crank the vibrance slider and call it a day. It's like they've never seen a real human being before. 

But anyway, yeah, I do that checking thing. Like I said, it doesn't take over my whole day or anything, but it does make me slower. And I just feel less free creatively, you know? Like I'm second-guessing myself constantly.
Would you say that these nagging thoughts about your work are causing you a lot of emotional pain or discomfort?

Um, emotional pain? I don't know if I'd call it pain. It's more just... annoying, I guess? Like a mosquito buzzing in your ear when you're trying to sleep. Speaking of mosquitoes, the bugs this summer have been absolutely relentless. I tried sitting out on my patio with a glass of wine the other night, and I swear I was out there for five minutes before I got eaten alive. I had to go back inside and hunt down this anti-itch cream I bought like three years ago. It was in the back of my medicine cabinet, behind all these half-empty bottles of vitamins I keep forgetting to take. I bought these gummy vitamins because I thought they'd be easier to remember, but they taste like artificial cherry, which is just the worst flavor. It reminds me of cough syrup from when I was a kid. My mom used to try to hide it in orange juice, but it just made the orange juice taste terrible. 

Actually, I was thinking about redesigning the packaging for a vitamin company. Their current branding is so medicinal and sterile. If they made it look more like a lifestyle product, like those fancy adaptogen powders you see all over Instagram, they could probably charge double. It's all about perceived value. I pitched that idea to my creative director, but he's so old-school. He still thinks everything needs a giant logo and a bright red "NEW!" burst on the front. 

But um, what were you asking? Oh, if the thoughts cause me pain. Yeah, no, not really pain. Just... discomfort, maybe? It's just frustrating because it slows me down. But it's not like I'm crying over it or anything. It's just a mild annoyance, really.
Are these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors significantly interfering with your ability to function at work or enjoy your free time?

Um, interfering? I mean, I'm still getting my work done. It's not like I'm completely paralyzed or anything. But, um... I have started missing a few internal deadlines lately. Which is so unlike me, because usually I'm the one badgering the copywriters to get their text to me on time. Copywriters are the worst with deadlines, I swear. They always want just one more day to "finesse the messaging," and I'm like, guys, the printer needs the files by 5 PM, they don't care about your brilliant pun. I used to work with this one writer, Dave, who would literally send me revisions while I was exporting the final PDF. He drove me absolutely crazy. But he brought in donuts every Friday, so we tolerated him. The good kind of donuts, too, from that little bakery on 4th Street with the maple bacon bars. Oh my god, I haven't had one of those in months. I should really go there this weekend. Although parking around there is a nightmare now that they put in those new bike lanes. I mean, I'm all for cycling, but they took away half the street parking, and it's impossible to find a spot. 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, so I'm missing some internal deadlines because of the checking. And honestly, I'm holding back on my bolder design ideas. I'm just so afraid I'll overlook some tiny detail if I try something new, and I really want to move toward a creative director role eventually. So I'm playing it safe, which... yeah, I guess that is interfering a bit with how I want my career to go. But I'm still functioning, you know? Just... maybe not as well as I could be.
Would you say that these nagging thoughts about your work are causing you significant distress?

Um, significant distress? I feel like... wait, didn't you just ask me about emotional pain? Is distress different? I mean, I guess it's basically the same thing, right? Like I said before, it's not like I'm crying or having panic attacks over it. It's just that annoying feeling, like the mosquito. Or like when you buy a brand new sweater and you realize there's a tiny pull in the thread right on the front, and you can't unsee it. I bought this beautiful cashmere blend last week—emerald green, which is totally my color—and I wore it to the office once, just once, and caught it on the edge of my desk. Our desks are these reclaimed wood things that look amazing but are completely impractical because they splinter if you look at them wrong. They spent thousands of dollars outfitting the whole open-plan office with them, but they didn't invest in decent chairs, which makes absolutely no sense. If you're sitting at a desk for nine hours a day, you need lumbar support, not a cute aesthetic. I ended up bringing in my own lumbar pillow from home. It's this ugly orthopedic gray thing, but it saves my back. 

But um, distress... yeah, no, I wouldn't call it significant distress. It's just... it's just frustrating. It's an annoyance. I'm not, like, falling apart over it.
Do you feel like you must perform these checking behaviors to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, prevent something bad? I mean, I guess I just don't want to make a mistake. So before I submit my work now, I'll re-open the file, compare all the layers, re-save it, and then I kind of mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. It's not like it takes over my whole day, but it definitely makes me slower. And less free creatively, like I mentioned before. I used to be so fast, you know? Like, I could whip up a mock-up in an hour. My first boss out of college used to call me "Lightning." He was this great guy, ran a boutique agency out of a converted warehouse downtown. The rent there must have been astronomical, but the lighting was incredible. Huge floor-to-ceiling windows. Of course, in the winter it was freezing. We all had to wear fingerless gloves to type. I bought this pair of really cute wool ones from a craft fair, but they were so itchy I ended up just keeping a space heater under my desk. Space heaters are technically a fire hazard, I think, but everyone had one. The building's wiring was probably from the 1920s anyway, so if it was going to burn down, it wouldn't have been my little heater that did it. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, preventing something bad. Yeah, I just don't want a typo or a misaligned graphic to go to print. So I just do my little routine—check the layers, re-save, mentally review it all. It just takes a little extra time, that's all.
Are you finding it difficult to fulfill your responsibilities at work or maintain relationships with friends and family because of these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um, difficult to fulfill responsibilities? I feel like we just talked about this, didn't we? With the work stuff? I mean, I'm still getting my work done. It's not like I'm dropping the ball completely or getting fired. But yeah, like I said, I've started missing some internal deadlines. And I'm definitely holding back on my bolder design ideas. I'm just so afraid I'll overlook something if I try a new layout or experiment with typography, and I really don't want to damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role. I've wanted to be a creative director since I was, like, twenty-five. I remember seeing this documentary about the guy who designed the original Apple packaging, and it just blew my mind. The way they thought about the unboxing experience as a physical journey? Genius. I actually tried to implement something like that for a client last year—a boutique skincare line—but their budget was way too tight for custom die-cuts. Clients always want champagne packaging on a beer budget. They show you a Pinterest board full of embossed foil and soft-touch laminate, and then tell you they can only afford standard four-color printing on flimsy cardstock. It's so depressing. I had this one client, a local kombucha brand, who wanted their labels to look like they were hand-painted by monks or something, but wouldn't even pay for a decent illustrator. I ended up doing the watercolor elements myself on a Sunday afternoon. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, friends and family. Um, I mean, I guess I'm a little more tired after work because the checking takes up mental energy, so maybe I say no to happy hours a bit more often. But mostly it's just the work stuff—the deadlines and playing it safe with my designs.
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or perform specific rituals when you're having these nagging thoughts about your work?

Um, didn't I just tell you about this? With the files? I feel like I just went over my whole routine a minute ago. But yeah, if I get those nagging thoughts, I do exactly what I said before—I'll re-open the file, compare all the layers, re-save it, and then mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. 

It's all about checking the layers, honestly. Though, speaking of layers, the new Adobe update completely ruined how the layer groups work. I had my workspace set up perfectly for, like, five years, and then they just force this update on you overnight. It's ridiculous. You pay an absolute fortune for the Creative Cloud subscription every month now. It used to just be a flat fee for the software on a disc, remember that? I actually still have my old CS6 discs in a box somewhere. I can't bring myself to throw them away because the packaging was really nice. They had this cool geometric artwork on the front, very mid-2000s tech vibe. I think I kept the box in my hall closet next to my old college portfolios. My mom tried to throw them out last Thanksgiving when she came to visit because she said they were just gathering dust, but I told her you never know when you might need a physical backup. Plus, she's one to talk, she has a whole garage full of antique lamps she swears she's going to rewire someday. She buys them at estate sales and then they just sit there.

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, repeating actions. Yeah, so, I don't know if I'd call it a ritual exactly, but I just have to do that whole checking and saving process before I send anything off. Like I mentioned, it doesn't take over my entire day or anything, but it definitely makes me slower. It just makes me feel way less free creatively.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with friends and family or perform daily tasks because of these nagging thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um, harder to enjoy time with friends and family or perform daily tasks? I swear we just went over this, didn't we? I mean, I feel like I'm repeating myself here. But like I said before, I'm still getting my work done. It's not like I'm totally failing at my job. But yeah, I've started missing those internal deadlines, and I'm definitely holding back on my bolder design ideas. I'm just terrified I'll overlook a mistake if I try something new, and I really don't want to damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role. 

Which is so frustrating because I've been working toward that promotion for literally years. The current creative director, Marcus, he's great, but he's been talking about retiring to upstate New York for like three years now. He bought this gorgeous mid-century modern fixer-upper near Beacon. He showed me pictures of the original wood paneling in the living room, and it is stunning. I love mid-century design. I actually went to this amazing vintage furniture market last weekend looking for a teak credenza for my apartment. They had some incredible pieces, but the prices were just insane. I saw this one Eames-style lounge chair that was completely falling apart, like the leather was cracked and the foam was crumbling, and the guy still wanted twelve hundred dollars for it. I ended up just buying a little ceramic planter instead. It has this really cute geometric pattern on it, kind of reminds me of those old software boxes I was telling you about earlier. I put a pothos plant in it, but I'm notoriously bad at keeping plants alive. I always either overwater them or completely forget they exist. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, friends and family. Yeah, like I said, I'm just a little more tired after work because of all the mental energy I spend checking things, so maybe I skip a happy hour here and there. But the main thing is really just the work stuff—missing those internal deadlines and playing it safe with my designs because I want that promotion so badly.

Hi, thanks. Um, well, I came in because I keep having these... these really nagging thoughts about my work. I'm a graphic designer, and honestly, lately the whole process has just been so chaotic. Like, the new software updates they keep pushing out? Total nightmare. patient.answer:
Um, difficult to fulfill responsibilities? I feel like we just talked about this, didn't we? With the work stuff? I mean, I'm still getting my work done. It's not like I'm dropping the ball completely or getting fired. But yeah, like I said, I've started missing some internal deadlines. And I'm definitely holding back on my bolder design ideas. I'm just so afraid I'll overlook something if I try a new layout or experiment with typography, and I really don't want to damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role. I've wanted to be a creative director since I was, like, twenty-five. I remember seeing this documentary about the guy who designed the original Apple packaging, and it just blew my mind. The way they thought about the unboxing experience as a physical journey? Genius. I actually tried to implement something like that for a client last year—a boutique skincare line—but their budget was way too tight for custom die-cuts. Clients always want champagne packaging on a beer budget. They show you a Pinterest board full of embossed foil and soft-touch laminate, and then tell you they can only afford standard four-color printing on flimsy cardstock. It's so depressing. I had this one client, a local kombucha brand, who wanted their labels to look like they were hand-painted by monks or something, but wouldn't even pay for a decent illustrator. I ended up doing the watercolor elements myself on a Sunday afternoon. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, friends and family. Um, I mean, I guess I'm a little more tired after work because the checking takes up mental energy, so maybe I say no to happy hours a bit more often. But mostly it's just the work stuff—the deadlines and playing it safe with my designs.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) by asking about the presence of compulsions to perform specific rituals or behaviors
doctor.question: Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or perform specific rituals when you're having these nagging thoughts about your work?

target_item.name: Compulsions
target_item.manifestation: Before I submit work now, I’ll re-open the file, compare the layers, re-save it, and sometimes mentally walk through every design choice one more time, which doesn’t take over my whole day but does make me slower and less free creatively.

patient.answer:
Um, didn't I just tell you about this? With the files? I feel like I just went over my whole routine a minute ago. But yeah, if I get those nagging thoughts, I do exactly what I said before—I'll re-open the file, compare all the layers, re-save it, and then mentally walk through every single design choice one more time. 

It's all about checking the layers, honestly. Though, speaking of layers, the new Adobe update completely ruined how the layer groups work. I had my workspace set up perfectly for, like, five years, and then they just force this update on you overnight. It's ridiculous. You pay an absolute fortune for the Creative Cloud subscription every month now. It used to just be a flat fee for the software on a disc, remember that? I actually still have my old CS6 discs in a box somewhere. I can't bring myself to throw them away because the packaging was really nice. They had this cool geometric artwork on the front, very mid-2000s tech vibe. I think I kept the box in my hall closet next to my old college portfolios. My mom tried to throw them out last Thanksgiving when she came to visit because she said they were just gathering dust, but I told her you never know when you might need a physical backup. Plus, she's one to talk, she has a whole garage full of antique lamps she swears she's going to rewire someday. She buys them at estate sales and then they just sit there.

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, repeating actions. Yeah, so, I don't know if I'd call it a ritual exactly, but I just have to do that whole checking and saving process before I send anything off. Like I mentioned, it doesn't take over my entire day or anything, but it definitely makes me slower. It just makes me feel way less free creatively.

Um, harder to enjoy time with friends and family or perform daily tasks? I swear we just went over this, didn't we? I mean, I feel like I'm repeating myself here. But like I said before, I'm still getting my work done. It's not like I'm totally failing at my job. But yeah, I've started missing those internal deadlines, and I'm definitely holding back on my bolder design ideas. I'm just terrified I'll overlook a mistake if I try something new, and I really don't want to damage my chances of moving toward a creative director role. 

Which is so frustrating because I've been working toward that promotion for literally years. The current creative director, Marcus, he's great, but he's been talking about retiring to upstate New York for like three years now. He bought this gorgeous mid-century modern fixer-upper near Beacon. He showed me pictures of the original wood paneling in the living room, and it is stunning. I love mid-century design. I actually went to this amazing vintage furniture market last weekend looking for a teak credenza for my apartment. They had some incredible pieces, but the prices were just insane. I saw this one Eames-style lounge chair that was completely falling apart, like the leather was cracked and the foam was crumbling, and the guy still wanted twelve hundred dollars for it. I ended up just buying a little ceramic planter instead. It has this really cute geometric pattern on it, kind of reminds me of those old software boxes I was telling you about earlier. I put a pothos plant in it, but I'm notoriously bad at keeping plants alive. I always either overwater them or completely forget they exist. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, friends and family. Yeah, like I said, I'm just a little more tired after work because of all the mental energy I spend checking things, so maybe I skip a happy hour here and there.
